--- See a feature in an app that you want in your own product? Ask your agent to investigate it with REA. It can inspect the app without its source code, explain how the feature works, show the evidence, and build a version for your project. REA connects your agent to tools for inspecting native binaries, JavaScript and Electron apps, .NET assemblies, and websites. You can also use the same tools from your terminal. Analysis runs locally, and results include the evidence and limitations behind each conclusion. Setup registers REA with your agent and installs matching workflow instructions. Native analysis can use an existing Hopper, Ghidra, or IDA installation; setup can optionally install Hopper with approval. Static JavaScript analysis needs no native analysis engine. > **[Visit the REA website](https://rea.tools/)** for setup instructions, illustrated guides, and real case studies. ## Quick start On Linux, Ghidra, JADX, firmware tool launches and static JavaScript/Electron analysis require a procps-compatible `ps` on REA's `PATH` for process ownership checks. Recovery steps are in `docs/installation.md` under "Linux owned-process prerequisite". ### Set up your agent With Node.js and npm installed, run: ```bash npx rea-agents setup ``` Choose your agents, review the proposed changes, and approve them. Setup adds REA's MCP server and matching workflow instructions, with backups of existing configuration. Restart your agent afterward. Setup supports Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, Grok Build and [other agents](docs/installation.md#supported-agents). See [installation and setup](docs/installation.md) for provider configuration and manual MCP registration. MCP uses compact input schemas by default to reduce context overhead. Set `REA_MCP_INPUT_SCHEMA_PROFILE=full` in your MCP registration when you need the complete advertised field guidance and nested validation details. Both profiles keep the full tool set and canonical server validation. See "Compact input schema profile" in the MCP contracts guide. ### Ask your agent ```text Understand how search works in the Notes app, show me the evidence, and build a similar feature for my project. ``` Replace Notes with your target app and the feature you want to understand. ### Use the terminal Inspect an extracted JavaScript/Electron app directory or ASAR: ```bash npx -y rea-agents@latest analyze-javascript-application /absolute/path/to/app --json ``` The result includes modules, imports, Electron boundaries and their evidence. Replace the path with your target, such as `"D:/apps/example"` on Windows. To install the `rea` command for regular use: ```bash npm install --global rea-agents rea --help ``` For native analysis, configure a provider first. See the [CLI and Evidence guide](docs/cli.md) for native commands, provider selection, snapshots and scripting. ### Update REA REA changes quickly, and new releases include frequent bug fixes. Keep your installation up to date. For a CLI installed with `npm install --global` or `bun add --global`: ```bash rea update ``` `rea --update` is an alias for this verified workflow and accepts the same global output flags. Use `rea update` when combining it with other command controls. Updater commands retain at most 4 MiB of stdout and stderr combined. Oversized metadata replies are rejected after the command exits; verbose installs continue with bounded diagnostics. Human progress output respects terminal backpressure and waits for submitted writes to finish. Bun global updates require Bun 1.2.17 or later. With an older Bun release, upgrade Bun manually before running `rea update`. To refresh your agent registrations and skill, run the setup command printed by the update. If you use `npx`, update your agent setup with: ```bash npx rea-agents@latest setup ``` Review the setup changes and restart your agent. For one-off CLI commands, use `npx rea-agents@latest` followed by the command. With Bun, use `bunx rea-agents@latest` in place of `npx rea-agents@latest`. ## How REA works Your agent calls REA through MCP to inspect the target and trace relevant code. REA returns findings with their evidence. The agent uses them to ask follow-up questions, explain the behavior, or write and test an implementation. CLI commands use the same workflows. ![REA investigation flow: your agent asks about a local target, REA inspects and traces it using analysis tools, and the agent uses the returned code, references and unknowns to explain, implement and test.](website/public/assets/figures/rea-investigation-flow.svg) [Open the full-size figure](website/public/assets/figures/rea-investigation-flow.svg). """Minimal Android boot image (header v0/v1/v2) unpacker + ikconfig/vmlinux extraction."""
import struct, sys, os, gzip, io, subprocess

def rd(f, off, n):
    f.seek(off)
    return f.read(n)

def unpack(path, outdir):
    os.makedirs(outdir, exist_ok=True)
    size = os.path.getsize(path)
    with open(path, 'rb') as f:
        hdr = rd(f, 0, 1632)
    magic = hdr[:8]
    print(f"file={path} size={size} magic={magic!r}")
    if magic != b'ANDROID!':
        print("not ANDROID! (may be Samsung zImage-only or different format)")
        return None
    (ksize, kaddr, rsize, raddr, ssize, saddr, tags, page,
     field9, osver) = struct.unpack_from('<10I', hdr, 8)
    name = hdr[48:64].split(b'\0')[0]
    cmdline = hdr[64:576].split(b'\0')[0]
    extra = hdr[592:1616].split(b'\0')[0]
    hv = field9 if field9 in (0, 1, 2) else 0
    dt_size = field9 if hv == 0 else 0
    print(f"kernel={ksize} ramdisk={rsize} second={ssize} dt={dt_size} page={page} hdrver={hv}")
    print(f"name={name!r}\ncmdline={cmdline.decode('utf-8','replace')}\nextra={extra.decode('utf-8','replace')}")
    if page == 0 or page > 65536:
        print("bad page size"); return None
    pos = page
    def take(n, nm):
        nonlocal pos
        if n == 0:
            print(f"{nm}: empty"); return b''
        data = rd(f, pos, n)
        padded = (n + page - 1) // page * page
        pos += padded
        print(f"{nm}: off={pos-padded} len={n} -> {nm}.bin")
        open(os.path.join(outdir, nm + '.bin'), 'wb').write(data)
        return data
    kern = take(ksize, 'kernel')
    take(rsize, 'ramdisk')
    take(ssize, 'second')
    if hv == 0 and dt_size:
        take(dt_size, 'dt')
    elif hv >= 1:
        # v1: recovery_dtbo_size, recovery_dtbo_offset, header_size ; v2 adds dtb_size, dtb_addr
        hdr2 = rd(f, 1632, 16)
        rd_size, rd_off = struct.unpack_from('<II', hdr2, 0)
        print(f"recovery_dtbo size={rd_size} off={rd_off}")
        if hv == 2:
            (dtb_size, dtb_addr) = struct.unpack_from('<IQ', rd(f, 1648, 12), 0)
            print(f"dtb size={dtb_size} addr={dtb_addr:#x}")
    return {'kernel': kern, 'page': page}

MAGICS = [
    (b'\x1f\x8b\x08', 'gzip'),
    (b'\xfd7zXZ\x00', 'xz'),
    (b'\x04\x22\x4d\x18', 'lz4'),
    (b'\x28\xb5\x2f\xfd', 'zstd'),
    (b'\x89LZO\x00\r\n\x1a\n', 'lzo'),
    (b'\x5d\x00\x00', 'lzma'),
]

def decompress_any(data, nm, outdir):
    for magic, kind in MAGICS:
        i = data.find(magic)
        while i != -1:
            try:
                if kind == 'gzip':
                    out = gzip.decompress(data[i:])
                elif kind == 'xz':
                    import lzma; out = lzma.decompress(data[i:])
                elif kind == 'zstd':
                    out = subprocess.run(['zstd','-d','-c'], input=data[i:], capture_output=True).stdout
                elif kind == 'lz4':
                    out = subprocess.run(['lz4','-d','-c'], input=data[i:], capture_output=True).stdout
                else:
                    out = b''
                if len(out) > 1024*1024:
                    p = os.path.join(outdir, f'{nm}.{kind}')
                    open(p,'wb').write(out)
                    print(f"decompressed {kind} at off {i}: {len(out)} bytes -> {p}")
                    return out
            except Exception as e:
                pass
            i = data.find(magic, i+1)
    return None

def extract_ikconfig(kern, outdir):
    st = kern.find(b'IKCFG_ST')
    ed = kern.find(b'IKCFG_ED', st if st != -1 else 0)
    print(f"IKCFG_ST={st} IKCFG_ED={ed}")
    if st != -1 and ed > st:
        blob = kern[st+8:ed]
        for kind, fn in (('gzip', lambda b: gzip.decompress(b)),
                         ('xz', lambda b: __import__('lzma').decompress(b)),
                         ('lz4', lambda b: subprocess.run(['lz4','-d','-c'], input=b, capture_output=True).stdout)):
            try:
                cfg = fn(blob)
                if b'CONFIG_' in cfg:
                    p = os.path.join(outdir, 'config')
                    open(p,'wb').write(cfg)
                    print(f"ikconfig {kind} -> {p} ({len(cfg)} bytes)")
                    return cfg
            except Exception as e:
                print(f"ikconfig {kind} failed: {e}")
    return None

if __name__ == '__main__':
    src, outdir = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
    r = unpack(src, outdir)
    if r:
        kern = r['kernel']
        extract_ikconfig(kern, outdir)
        decompress_any(kern, 'vmlinux', outdir)
"}

**postmarketOS, the mobile Linux distribution based on Alpine Linux, is changing its name to Nura.**


The rename was announced at a community conference on 27 September, [after an 18-month selection process](https://docs.postmarketos.org/pmcr/main/0003-name-change-plan.html) .


[The team said the change](https://nura.eco/blog/2026/09/27/nura-rename/) was driven partly by the difficulty of using “postmarketOS”. 
The name is five syllables long and difficult to pronounce in many languages, while its capitalisation has also resulted in variants including “PostmarketOS”, “Postmarketos” and “post-market OS”.


Nura logo for former postmarketOS project New name, tweaked logo

As a purely descriptive name, the team argue that it could not be trademarked. 
The “post-market” framing is no longer felt to fully reflect the project’s status, not now it has its own hardware partners, like PINE64, who ship hardware with the OS pre-installed.

## Development status

### Sources used

[Lineage OS kernel sources for Exynos 7580 Devices](https://github.com/LineageOS/android_kernel_samsung_universal7580)

### Compiles

- Linux kernel 3.10.108
- Device information

### What's working

- Hardcoded kernel arguments
- Making a Nura Recovery zip
- Flashing using custom recovery
- Showing splash screen during boot
- Starting full X-Session and using the UI with USB-OTG Keyboard and Mouse
- Running LXQt or SXMO

### What's wrong

- *When the phone boots it shows the splash screen meaning the rendering is working. But it crashes and force reboots soon after. - This is probably caused due to the fact that the init is messed up because the bootloader passes the wrong kernel arguments. The ones that are used to boot android.* - But this issue has been fixed
- Being unable to mount the system partitions in TWRP to check logs or modify the system because normally Nura images are two images packed together.(Later initfs and rootfs) And TWRP cant mount it because TWRP doesnt have the necessary tools. While using split images generally work, some TWRP builds may have issues mounting EXT4 partitions.
- Display manager not showing up after starting up
- WiFi and Bluetooth hardware not being detected or initialized.
- LightDM Failing to start properly. Causing it to not boot into desktop automatically

## How to enter flash mode

Power down the device first.

#### ODIN/Heimdall Mode

To enter ODIN/Heimdall flashing mode, press and hold Power + Home + Volume Down buttons until a warning screen pops up. Then press Volume Up button to enter ODIN mode.

#### Recovery (Stock/Custom) Mode

To enter Recovery (Stock/Custom) mode, press and hold Power + Home + Volume Up buttons until the Recovery splash screen pops up.

## Installation

Perform the standard installation method provided by [PostMarket OS Installation Guide](https://wiki.nura.eco/wiki/Installation_guide)

But keep in mind that...

| ![Warning](/images/9/9d/Red_warning_icon.svg) | **WARNING:** Installation with Heimdall partially works. It is recommended to use the custom recovery method provided by [Nura Wiki](https://wiki.nura.eco/wiki/Installation_from_recovery_mode) to install it. |

content.text:
#!/bin/sh

# Parse arguments
builddir=$1
pkgdir=$2
_carch=$3
_flavor=$4
_outdir=$5

if [ -z "$builddir" ] || [ -z "$pkgdir" ] || [ -z "$_carch" ] ||
	[ -z "$_flavor" ]; then
	echo "ERROR: missing argument!"
	echo "Please call downstreamkernel_package() with \$builddir, \$pkgdir,"
	echo "\$_carch, \$_flavor (and optionally \$_outdir) as arguments."
	exit 1
fi

# kernel.release
install -D "$builddir/$_outdir/include/config/kernel.release" \
	"$pkgdir/usr/share/kernel/$_flavor/kernel.release"

# zImage (find the right one)
# shellcheck disable=SC2164
cd "$builddir/$_outdir/arch/$_carch/boot"
_target="$pkgdir/boot/vmlinuz"

if [ -n "$KERNEL_IMAGE_NAME" ]; then
	if ! [ -e "$KERNEL_IMAGE_NAME" ]; then
		echo "Could not find \$KERNEL_IMAGE_NAME in $PWD!"
		exit 1
	else
		echo "NOTE: using $KERNEL_IMAGE_NAME as kernel image."
		install -Dm644 "$KERNEL_IMAGE_NAME" "$_target"
	fi
else
	for _zimg in zImage-dtb Image.gz-dtb *zImage Image; do
		[ -e "$_zimg" ] || continue
		echo "zImage found: $_zimg"
		install -Dm644 "$_zimg" "$_target"
		break
	done
	if ! [ -e "$_target" ]; then
		echo "Could not find zImage in $PWD!"
		exit 1
	fi
fi

Decide whether Nura's modem kernel stack is at parity with the ROM and identify the firmware/userspace boundary. Owned paths for kernel edits: `drivers/misc/modem_v1/**` (tree root below). Do not edit shared DT; report deltas.

## Known evidence
- ROM symbols: 23 `modem_*`, 62 total with `shm_*`/sipc; Nura tree has `drivers/misc/modem_v1` and config `CONFIG_SEC_MODEM_V1=y`, `CONFIG_SEC_MODEM_SS310AP=y`, `CONFIG_EXYNOS7580_SHM_IPC=y`, `CONFIG_EXYNOS7580_MCU_IPC=y`.
- ROM DT `sec_modem,modem_pdata`, `samsung,exynos7580-shm_ipc`; Nura DT nodes are present (verify exactly).
- The modem firmware lives in the CP tar (`CP_J700MUBU2BRC1...tar.md5` inside the original zip), not in AP. The kernel driver's firmware load is via a userspace ioctl (`modem_io_device.c` uses a user buffer). Determine the exact files the userspace must supply and from which CP partition/file.
- Nura wiki says calls/SMS/data are untested; no RIL in Nura.

## Work
1. P1: hidden-symbol coverage for `modem_v1` and the 7580 IPC; explain `shm_*`/generic misses. Real gaps only (objdump if a vendor function is truly missing).
2. P2: compare modem/SHM/IPC DT nodes/properties (regions, interrupts, GPIOs, clocks). List deltas.
3. P3: verify config/dependencies.
4. P4: inspect the CP tar (use `unzip -p` on the original zip; list contents). Map the modem/bootloader firmware files and determine what the kernel vs userspace needs. Produce `parity/firmware/files-modem.list` for any files the kernel/userspace expects.
5. State the userspace/RIL requirement and whether any kernel patch is warranted. Do not fabricate a kernel patch if the gap is userspace.

## Deliverables
- `parity/reports/modem.md` (P1-P4, CP tar inventory, verdict, residual risks).
- Patch only under `parity/patches/modem/` if a real kernel gap exists (apply-checked).
- `parity/firmware/files-modem.list` if applicable.
Return the JSON summary.

# Verify all parity patches apply cleanly against the baseline index.

#!/bin/sh
# Rebuild firmware.tar.gz for firmware-samsung-j7elte from the stock SM-J700M ROM.
#
# Usage: ./extract-firmware.sh <AP_J700MUBU2BRC2_*.tar.md5>
#
# Requires: tar, simg2img, debugfs, gzip, sha512sum.
# The tarball is deterministic (sorted, epoch mtimes), so the sha512 in the
# APKBUILD is reproducible.
set -eu

AP=${1:?usage: $0 <AP_J700MUBU2BRC2_*.tar.md5>}
here=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)
cd "$here"

work=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT

echo "extracting system.img from $AP ..."
tar -xf "$AP" -C "$work" system.img
simg2img "$work/system.img" "$work/system.raw"

# ROM path (inside system.img) -> local name
EXTRACT="
/etc/wifi/bcmdhd_sta.bin
/etc/wifi/bcmdhd_apsta.bin
/etc/wifi/bcmdhd_mfg.bin
/etc/wifi/nvram_net.txt
/etc/wifi/nvram_mfg.txt
/vendor/firmware/bcm43438A1_V0051.0230.hcd
/vendor/firmware/fimc_is_fd.bin
/vendor/firmware/fimc_is_fw2_3l2.bin
/vendor/firmware/mfc_fw.bin
/vendor/firmware/setfile_3l2.bin
/vendor/firmware/setfile_5e3.bin
"

rm -rf files
mkdir files
for src in $EXTRACT; do
	base=$(basename "$src")
	debugfs -R "dump $src files/$base" "$work/system.raw" >/dev/null 2>&1
	if [ ! -s "files/$base" ]; then
		echo "ERROR: $src not found in system.img" >&2
		exit 1
	fi
done

echo "verifying checksums ..."
(cd files && sha512sum -c ../files.sha512)

echo "building deterministic firmware.tar.gz ..."
(cd files && tar --sort=name --mtime=@0 --owner=0 --group=0 --numeric-owner -cf - *) |
	gzip -n > firmware.tar.gz
sha512sum firmware.tar.gz

}

	unset LDFLAGS
	make O="$_outdir" ARCH="$_carch" CC="${CC:-gcc}" \
		KBUILD_BUILD_VERSION="$((pkgrel + 1 ))-postmarketOS"

		"$_flavor" "$_outdir"
	install -Dm644 "$_outdir/arch/$_carch/boot"/dt.img \
		"$pkgdir"/boot/dt.img

#!/bin/sh
# Verify all parity patches apply cleanly against the baseline index of the
# right repository (kernel tree or pmaports), routed by the paths in the diff.
set -u
ROOT=/run/media/asdf/30620d0d-1e41-4d55-af08-b4de2fb9c517/j7rom
KT=$(ls -d "$ROOT"/android_kernel_samsung_universal7580-*)
PM="$ROOT/parity/pmaports"
fail=0
for p in "$ROOT"/parity/patches/*/*.patch; do
	[ -e "$p" ] || continue
	first=$(grep -m1 '^--- a/' "$p" | sed 's|^--- a/||; s|\t.*||')
	case "$first" in
	device/*) tree="$PM" ;;
	*) tree="$KT" ;;
	esac
	if git -C "$tree" apply --check --cached "$p" 2>/dev/null; then
		echo "OK   ${p#$ROOT/}  -> $(basename "$tree")"
	else
		echo "FAIL ${p#$ROOT/}  -> $(basename "$tree")"
		git -C "$tree" apply --check --cached "$p" 2>&1 | sed 's/^/     /'
		fail=1
	fi
done
exit $fail

# j7elte ROM <-> Nura driver parity session

Working directory for the Samsung Galaxy J7 (2015) `SM-J700M` (`j7elte`, Exynos 7580)
kernel driver parity work between the stock Android ROM and Nura (formerly postmarketOS).

## Device / sources

- Stock ROM: `SM-J700M` `J700MUBU2BRC2`, Android 6.0.1, kernel `3.10.61-13213628`.
- ROM kernel: raw arm64 `Image`, all drivers built in (no `.ko` modules),
  55,634 kallsyms symbols recovered.
- Nura kernel: `LineageOS/android_kernel_samsung_universal7580` @ `2a746c1`,
  downstream 3.10.108, baseline commit `b5e363a`. Nura is **not** mainline for this device.
- Upstream reference: Linux 7.3 (kernel.org), used only for the parity survey.

## Layout

```
boot.img, recovery.img, system.img, system.raw   extracted ROM images
AP_J700MUBU2BRC2_..._user_low_ship.tar.md5       AP tar (extracted from the stock zip)
boot_out/                                        kernel.bin, vmlinux.elf, symbols.txt, dtbs/
android_kernel_samsung_universal7580-.../         Nura kernel tree (clean baseline)
linux-7.3/, linux-7.3.tar.xz                      upstream reference
toolchains/                                       GCC 10.3 aarch64 toolchain
config-nura-j7elte                                Nura build config (pristine)
lineage-kernel.tar.gz                             Nura kernel source archive
tools/                                            boot image / config comparison helpers
session/tmp-artifacts/                            scratch files moved out of /tmp
parity/                                           all deliverables (see below)
```

`parity/`:

```
patches/          7 exported patches (kernel + pmaports)
reports/          14 per-driver reports (P1-P4 evidence)
firmware/         extracted ROM blobs + per-driver file lists + MANIFEST.sha512
pmaports/         pmaports baseline ba682bd + uncommitted integration changes
build-src/        kernel worktree with build patches + parity kernel patches applied
out/              built Image and rev00/rev04/rev06 DTBs
build.sh          kernel build script (GCC 10.3)
verify.sh         applies every patch with git apply --check against the baselines
contract.md       parity definition and evidence rules
*.log             baseline / camera / final build logs
```

## Patches

Kernel (apply to the baseline kernel tree):

1. `parity/patches/bluetooth/0001-j7elte-bt-pinctrl.patch`
   - BT enable pin was `gpa1-6`; ROM uses `gpc4-2` on all three board revisions.
2. `parity/patches/camera/0001-fimc-is2-fallback-to-request_firmware-for-fw-version-check.patch`
   - FIMC-IS firmware version check hard-failed on `/system/vendor/firmware`;
     add a `request_firmware()` fallback so `/lib/firmware` works.

pmaports (apply in this order to `parity/pmaports`, baseline `ba682bd`):

3. `parity/patches/wifi/0001-j7elte-wifi-firmware-paths.patch`
   - `BCMDHD_FW_PATH` / `BCMDHD_NVRAM_PATH` -> `/lib/firmware/postmarketos/samsung-j7elte/`.
4. `parity/patches/bluetooth/0002-j7elte-bt-hci-config.patch`
   - enable `CONFIG_BT_HCIUART` + `CONFIG_BT_HCIUART_H4` for BlueZ `hciattach`/`btattach`.
5. `parity/patches/pmaports/0003-firmware-samsung-j7elte-package.patch`
   - new `firmware-samsung-j7elte` package (Wi-Fi, BT, FIMC-IS, MFC blobs).
6. `parity/patches/pmaports/0004-device-samsung-j7elte-depend-firmware.patch`
   - device package depends on the firmware package.
7. `parity/patches/pmaports/0005-linux-samsung-j7elte-config-sha512.patch`
   - updated config checksum after the two config changes.

Verify everything:

```
cd parity
./verify.sh          # all 7 patches -> OK
```

## Build

The ready-to-build worktree already contains the pmaports build patches (gcc8/gcc10,
fix-argb, etc.) plus the two parity kernel patches:

```
cd j7elte-session
./parity/build.sh parity/build-src parity/out Image dtbs
```

Outputs:

```
parity/out/arch/arm64/boot/Image
parity/out/arch/arm64/boot/dts/exynos7580-j7elte_rev00.dtb
parity/out/arch/arm64/boot/dts/exynos7580-j7elte_rev04.dtb
parity/out/arch/arm64/boot/dts/exynos7580-j7elte_rev06.dtb
```

Final build status: `BUILD_EXIT=0`, Image 17,365,040 bytes, three DTBs.
The camera fallback string and the `gpc4-2` BT pin group are present in the built outputs.

## Firmware package

`parity/pmaports/device/archived/firmware-samsung-j7elte/` contains:

- `APKBUILD` (deterministic `firmware.tar.gz`, sha512 pinned)
- `extract-firmware.sh` (rebuilds the tarball from the stock AP tar; verifies `files.sha512`)
- `files.sha512` (per-blob checksums)

Install destinations:

- `/lib/firmware/postmarketos/samsung-j7elte/` - bcmdhd firmware/NVRAM, BT HCD
- `/lib/firmware/` - `fimc_is_fw2_3l2.bin`, `setfile_3l2.bin`, `setfile_5e3.bin`,
  `fimc_is_fd.bin`, `mfc_fw.bin`

## Result

- 11 driver families at parity: display, battery, audio, sensors, storage, touch,
  USB, GPS, GPU, platform (thermal/devfreq/IOMMU/cpufreq), modem.
- 3 driver families patched: Wi-Fi (config), Bluetooth (DT + config), camera (driver fallback).
- No new kernel driver was required; the ROM driver set is already present in the Nura fork.

Remaining gaps are userspace, not kernel drivers: audio UCM/mixer state, a BCM4752 GPS
daemon, `cbd`/RIL for telephony, Mesa/EGL for 3D, a power-supply daemon for battery, and
KMS/DRM for Wayland display managers (the kernel is fbdev-only, like the stock ROM).

## Notes

- The original stock zip remains at `/home/asdf/Downloads/SAMFW.COM_SM-J700M_PCW_J700MUBU2BRC2_fac.zip`.
- 218 scratch entries moved from `/tmp` to `session/tmp-artifacts/` (see `MANIFEST.txt`).
- Verification is static plus cross-build; no runtime test on the phone was possible here.

3. Provide a systemd unit (and OpenRC script if trivial) + APKBUILD `j7elte-sensors` under `parity/pmaports/device/archived/`.
4. Cross-compile the daemon (static or dynamic) with the aarch64 toolchain; include the compile command and result.

## Acceptance
Compiles; D-Bus introspection XML/interface documented; reads the real driver interfaces; no fake sensor values. Hardware test steps documented.

# Driver: new DRM/KMS driver for Exynos7580 DECON + DSIM + ea8061 panel

## Goal
Create a new DRM/KMS driver in the Nura 3.10.108 kernel so standard KMS compositors can modeset the j7elte 720x1280 ea8061 panel. Today the kernel has only the vendor fbdev DECON driver (`drivers/video/exynos/decon_7580`), and CONFIG_DRM is off.

## Work
1. Study the vendor 7580 driver: `decon_core.c`, `decon_reg_7580.c`, `decon-int_drv.c`, `dpu_reg_7580.c`, `dsim_drv.c`, `dsim_reg_7580.c`, `panels/ea8061_lcd_ctrl.c`, `panels/ea8061_param.h`. Extract the real register offsets, clock/power sequencing and panel init commands.
2. Study the 3.10 DRM core and the existing `drivers/gpu/drm/exynos` framework; decide whether to extend it with a 7580 CRTC/encoder/connector or add a standalone DRM driver. Use the legacy CRTC helpers available in 3.10; do not assume atomic helpers.
3. Implement the driver: DECON CRTC + primary plane, DSIM encoder + connector, ea8061 panel init from the vendor sequence, dumb buffer allocation and fbdev emulation. Use the DT nodes/clock/regulator/power-domain data already present.
4. Add Kconfig/Makefile entries, a DT patch (new compatibles or a status switch), and a config fragment enabling DRM + the new driver and disabling the vendor fbdev display path.
5. Build with `parity/build.sh parity/build-src parity/out-drm Image dtbs` after applying the config fragment to a copy of the build config. Iterate until it compiles. Record the exact command and result.
6. If the full modeset cannot be completed, implement the maximum verified subset (probe, register map, clocks/power, panel init, connector detection) and document exactly what remains. Do not fake success.

## Acceptance
New source + Kconfig/Makefile + DT + config patches under `parity/patches/drm/`; build log; `parity/reports/drm-driver.md` with design, register sources, status and hardware test plan. No stubs returning success.

Return JSON.

tasks.task:
# Gap: reverse-engineer the BCM4752 init protocol from the ROM gpsd

Read `parity/reports/gps-userspace.md`. The kernel side and NMEA forwarder exist; the missing piece is the proprietary BCM4752 init/handshake.

## Work
1. Extract `/system/bin/gpsd` (Broadcom glgps) from `system.raw` via debugfs. It is an ELF32 ARM bionic binary, stripped, but C++ RTTI/string names are present (`GlMeSrdAsicinit::Bri_SendAutobaud`, `Bri_GetOutOfLegacy`, `Bri_RequestHwVersion`, `TXcrc`, `RXcrc`, `TXseq`, `RXseq`, etc.).
2. Use `aarch64`/`arm` objdump, `strings`, and Ghidra headless (`/opt/ghidra/support/analyzeHeadless`) to locate those functions and reconstruct:
   - the byte/packet framing (length, CRC polynomial/seed, sequence numbering, message IDs),
   - the autobaud pattern and legacy-exit sequence,
   - the hardware-version request and any required response,
   - whether the chip emits NMEA after this handshake.
3. If a complete init sequence is derived, update `parity/userspace/gps/src/j7elte-gpsd.c` to send it (behind a `--init` flag) and document it. If not, produce a precise blocker report with the addresses/disassembly evidence and what hardware capture would resolve it.
4. Update `parity/reports/gps-userspace.md` and the patches.

Do not fabricate protocol bytes; every byte/field must be traced to disassembly or a string. No hardware.
Return JSON.

data.report:
Reviewed the loader against drivers/misc/modem_v1 and re-disassembled the stock ARM32 /sbin/cbd with capstone to re-check the boot protocol. Found and fixed one real protocol bug plus one documentation defect:

1) Missing CP acknowledgements (protocol bug). cbd's stage loop (0x1cdcc) reads two unsolicited response words that the loader skipped: (stage<<8)|0xA001 after the LAST data frame of every data stage (no write; std_udl_req_resp(fd,0,...) at 0x1d016), and (stage<<8)|0xA00C after the CRC frame (0x1d0c6). Without them the RX queue would hold stale words and the following DONE handshake (expects 0xA00D) would read 0xA001/0xA00C and abort. Added wait_resp() and calls after the frame loop and after the CRC frame; dry-run logs both. Also re-confirmed the rest of the sequence against cbd: ioctl order MODEM_ON(0x6f19)->BOOT_ON(0x6f22)->DL_START(0x6f28), stage table (0 BOOT done-only; 1 TOC start+data+done, no CRC; 2 MAIN start+data+CRC+done; 3 NV start+data+done; 15 START-only), FW_UPDATE {stage_size, mtu=0x810, ceil(size/0x800)} once per data stage, 16-byte {cmd,num_frames,seq,len} frames with one write() each, CRC {cmd,crc}. XMIT_BOOT 28-byte packed ABI (0x6f40) matches the Nura kernel (shmem_xmit_boot copies sizeof(struct modem_firmware), u64 binary).

2) Wrong comment fixed: the header claimed the kernel adds no SIPC5 framing to the BOOT channel. #!/bin/sh
# Build the Nura j7elte 3.10.108 kernel with the GCC 10 ARM toolchain.
# Usage: build.sh <source-tree> <build-dir> [make-target...]
# Optional: CONFIG_FRAGMENT=<file> appends a Kconfig fragment to the baseline
# config before olddefconfig (e.g. parity/patches/drm/config-drm-exynos7580.fragment).
set -eu
SRC=$(realpath "${1:?source tree}")
OUT=$(realpath -m "${2:?build dir}")
shift 2 || true
TARGETS=${*:-Image dtbs}
TC=/run/media/asdf/30620d0d-1e41-4d55-af08-b4de2fb9c517/j7elte-session/toolchains/gcc-arm-10.3-2021.07-x86_64-aarch64-none-linux-gnu/bin

if [ -n "${CONFIG_FRAGMENT:-}" ]; then

# j7elte ROM <-> Nura driver parity session

Working directory for the Samsung Galaxy J7 (2015) `SM-J700M` (`j7elte`, Exynos 7580)
kernel driver parity work between the stock Android ROM and Nura (formerly postmarketOS).

## Device / sources

- Stock ROM: `SM-J700M` `J700MUBU2BRC2`, Android 6.0.1, kernel `3.10.61-13213628`.
- ROM kernel: raw arm64 `Image`, all drivers built in (no `.ko` modules),
  55,634 kallsyms symbols recovered.
- Nura kernel: `LineageOS/android_kernel_samsung_universal7580` @ `2a746c1`,
  downstream 3.10.108, baseline commit `b5e363a`. Nura is **not** mainline for this device.
- Upstream reference: Linux 7.3 (kernel.org), used only for the parity survey.

## Layout

```
boot.img, recovery.img, system.img, system.raw   extracted ROM images
AP_J700MUBU2BRC2_..._user_low_ship.tar.md5       AP tar (extracted from the stock zip)
boot_out/                                        kernel.bin, vmlinux.elf, symbols.txt, dtbs/
android_kernel_samsung_universal7580-.../         Nura kernel tree (clean baseline)
linux-7.3/, linux-7.3.tar.xz                      upstream reference
toolchains/                                       GCC 10.3 aarch64 toolchain
config-nura-j7elte                                Nura build config (pristine)
lineage-kernel.tar.gz                             Nura kernel source archive
tools/                                            boot image / config comparison helpers
session/tmp-artifacts/                            scratch files moved out of /tmp
parity/                                           all deliverables (see below)
```

`parity/`:

```
patches/          7 exported patches (kernel + pmaports)
reports/          14 per-driver reports (P1-P4 evidence)
firmware/         extracted ROM blobs + per-driver file lists + MANIFEST.sha512
pmaports/         pmaports baseline ba682bd + uncommitted integration changes
build-src/        kernel worktree with build patches + parity kernel patches applied
out/              built Image and rev00/rev04/rev06 DTBs
build.sh          kernel build script (GCC 10.3)
verify.sh         applies every patch with git apply --check against the baselines
contract.md       parity definition and evidence rules
*.log             baseline / camera / final build logs
```

## Patches

Kernel (apply to the baseline kernel tree):

1. `parity/patches/bluetooth/0001-j7elte-bt-pinctrl.patch`
   - BT enable pin was `gpa1-6`; ROM uses `gpc4-2` on all three board revisions.
2. `parity/patches/camera/0001-fimc-is2-fallback-to-request_firmware-for-fw-version-check.patch`
   - FIMC-IS firmware version check hard-failed on `/system/vendor/firmware`;
     add a `request_firmware()` fallback so `/lib/firmware` works.

pmaports (apply in this order to `parity/pmaports`, baseline `ba682bd`):

3. `parity/patches/wifi/0001-j7elte-wifi-firmware-paths.patch`
   - `BCMDHD_FW_PATH` / `BCMDHD_NVRAM_PATH` -> `/lib/firmware/postmarketos/samsung-j7elte/`.
4. `parity/patches/bluetooth/0002-j7elte-bt-hci-config.patch`
   - enable `CONFIG_BT_HCIUART` + `CONFIG_BT_HCIUART_H4` for BlueZ `hciattach`/`btattach`.
5. `parity/patches/pmaports/0003-firmware-samsung-j7elte-package.patch`
   - new `firmware-samsung-j7elte` package (Wi-Fi, BT, FIMC-IS, MFC blobs).
6. `parity/patches/pmaports/0004-device-samsung-j7elte-depend-firmware.patch`
   - device package depends on the firmware package.
7. `parity/patches/pmaports/0005-linux-samsung-j7elte-config-sha512.patch`
   - updated config checksum after the two config changes.

Verify everything:

```
cd parity
./verify.sh          # all 7 patches -> OK
```

## Build

The ready-to-build worktree already contains the pmaports build patches (gcc8/gcc10,
fix-argb, etc.) plus the two parity kernel patches:

```
cd j7elte-session
./parity/build.sh parity/build-src parity/out Image dtbs
```

Outputs:

```
parity/out/arch/arm64/boot/Image
parity/out/arch/arm64/boot/dts/exynos7580-j7elte_rev00.dtb
parity/out/arch/arm64/boot/dts/exynos7580-j7elte_rev04.dtb
parity/out/arch/arm64/boot/dts/exynos7580-j7elte_rev06.dtb
```

Final build status: `BUILD_EXIT=0`, Image 17,365,040 bytes, three DTBs.
The camera fallback string and the `gpc4-2` BT pin group are present in the built outputs.

## Firmware package

`parity/pmaports/device/archived/firmware-samsung-j7elte/` contains:

- `APKBUILD` (deterministic `firmware.tar.gz`, sha512 pinned)
- `extract-firmware.sh` (rebuilds the tarball from the stock AP tar; verifies `files.sha512`)

# j7elte ROM <-> Nura driver parity session

Working directory for the Samsung Galaxy J7 (2015) `SM-J700M` (`j7elte`, Exynos 7580)
kernel driver parity work between the stock Android ROM and Nura (formerly postmarketOS).

## Device / sources

- Stock ROM: `SM-J700M` `J700MUBU2BRC2`, Android 6.0.1, kernel `3.10.61-13213628`.
- ROM kernel: raw arm64 `Image`, all drivers built in (no `.ko` modules),
  55,634 kallsyms symbols recovered.
- Nura kernel: `LineageOS/android_kernel_samsung_universal7580` @ `2a746c1`,
  downstream 3.10.108, baseline commit `b5e363a`. Nura is **not** mainline for this device.
- Upstream reference: Linux 7.3 (kernel.org), used only for the parity survey.

## Layout

```
boot.img, recovery.img, system.img, system.raw   extracted ROM images
AP_J700MUBU2BRC2_..._user_low_ship.tar.md5       AP tar (extracted from the stock zip)
boot_out/                                        kernel.bin, vmlinux.elf, symbols.txt, dtbs/
android_kernel_samsung_universal7580-.../         Nura kernel tree (clean baseline)
linux-7.3/, linux-7.3.tar.xz                      upstream reference
toolchains/                                       GCC 10.3 aarch64 toolchain
config-nura-j7elte                                Nura build config (pristine)
lineage-kernel.tar.gz                             Nura kernel source archive
tools/                                            boot image / config comparison helpers
session/tmp-artifacts/                            scratch files moved out of /tmp
parity/                                           all deliverables (see below)
```

`parity/`:

```
patches/          7 exported patches (kernel + pmaports)
reports/          14 per-driver reports (P1-P4 evidence)
firmware/         extracted ROM blobs + per-driver file lists + MANIFEST.sha512
pmaports/         pmaports baseline ba682bd + uncommitted integration changes
build-src/        kernel worktree with build patches + parity kernel patches applied
out/              built Image and rev00/rev04/rev06 DTBs
build.sh          kernel build script (GCC 10.3)
verify.sh         applies every patch with git apply --check against the baselines
contract.md       parity definition and evidence rules
*.log             baseline / camera / final build logs
```

## Patches

Kernel (apply to the baseline kernel tree):

1. `parity/patches/bluetooth/0001-j7elte-bt-pinctrl.patch`
   - BT enable pin was `gpa1-6`; ROM uses `gpc4-2` on all three board revisions.
2. `parity/patches/camera/0001-fimc-is2-fallback-to-request_firmware-for-fw-version-check.patch`
   - FIMC-IS firmware version check hard-failed on `/system/vendor/firmware`;
     add a `request_firmware()` fallback so `/lib/firmware` works.

pmaports (apply in this order to `parity/pmaports`, baseline `ba682bd`):

3. `parity/patches/wifi/0001-j7elte-wifi-firmware-paths.patch`
   - `BCMDHD_FW_PATH` / `BCMDHD_NVRAM_PATH` -> `/lib/firmware/postmarketos/samsung-j7elte/`.
4. `parity/patches/bluetooth/0002-j7elte-bt-hci-config.patch`
   - enable `CONFIG_BT_HCIUART` + `CONFIG_BT_HCIUART_H4` for BlueZ `hciattach`/`btattach`.
5. `parity/patches/pmaports/0003-firmware-samsung-j7elte-package.patch`
   - new `firmware-samsung-j7elte` package (Wi-Fi, BT, FIMC-IS, MFC blobs).
6. `parity/patches/pmaports/0004-device-samsung-j7elte-depend-firmware.patch`
   - device package depends on the firmware package.
7. `parity/patches/pmaports/0005-linux-samsung-j7elte-config-sha512.patch`
   - updated config checksum after the two config changes.

Verify everything:

```
cd parity
./verify.sh          # all 7 patches -> OK
```

## Build

The ready-to-build worktree already contains the pmaports build patches (gcc8/gcc10,
fix-argb, etc.) plus the two parity kernel patches:

```
cd j7elte-session
./parity/build.sh parity/build-src parity/out Image dtbs
```

Outputs:

```

parity/out/arch/arm64/boot/dts/exynos7580-j7elte_rev06.dtb
```

Final build status: `BUILD_EXIT=0`, Image 17,365,040 bytes, three DTBs.
The camera fallback string and the `gpc4-2` BT pin group are present in the built outputs.

## Firmware package

`parity/pmaports/device/archived/firmware-samsung-j7elte/` contains:

- `APKBUILD` (deterministic `firmware.tar.gz`, sha512 pinned)
- `extract-firmware.sh` (rebuilds the tarball from the stock AP tar; verifies `files.sha512`)
- `files.sha512` (per-blob checksums)

Install destinations:

- `/lib/firmware/postmarketos/samsung-j7elte/` - bcmdhd firmware/NVRAM, BT HCD
- `/lib/firmware/` - `fimc_is_fw2_3l2.bin`, `setfile_3l2.bin`, `setfile_5e3.bin`,
  `fimc_is_fd.bin`, `mfc_fw.bin`

## Kernel driver parity (first round)

- 11 driver families at parity: display, battery, audio, sensors, storage, touch,
  USB, GPS, GPU, platform (thermal/devfreq/IOMMU/cpufreq), modem.
- 3 driver families patched: Wi-Fi (config), Bluetooth (DT + config), camera (driver fallback).
- The ROM's driver set is already present in the Nura fork; no driver code was missing
  for those families.

## New DRM/KMS driver (display)

- `parity/patches/drm/0001-drm-exynos7580-decon-dsim-kms.patch`
  adds `drivers/gpu/drm/exynos7580/` (DECON CRTC/plane, DSIM encoder/connector,
  ea8061 panel init, dumb buffers + fbdev).
- `parity/patches/drm/0002-arm64-dts-exynos7580-j7elte-drm-display.patch`
  adds `samsung,exynos7580-decon-drm` / `samsung,exynos7580-dsim` to rev00/04/06.
- `parity/patches/drm/config-drm-exynos7580.fragment` enables DRM,
  `CONFIG_DRM_EXYNOS7580`, 32 MB CMA, and disables the vendor fbdev display path.
- Verified build: `parity/final-out/arch/arm64/boot/Image` (17,545,608 B) + three
  j7elte DTBs; `exynos7580_{drm,decon,dsim}.o` are built and the DTBs contain the
  new compatibles.
- Hardware-untested. Keep the vendor fbdev driver as the fallback until a real
  modeset is validated on the phone.

## Userspace gap packages

New pmaports packages, all pulled in by `device-samsung-j7elte` depends:

| Package | Gap | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `j7elte-audio-ucm` | UCM2 routing/mixer for COD3022X (54/54 controls validated) | implemented |
| `j7elte-wifi` | wpa_supplicant template, `/efs/wifi` MAC provisioning | implemented |
| `j7elte-bt` | rfkill + hciattach + bluetoothd service, BCM43438A1.hcd | implemented |
| `j7elte-sensors` | K2HH/CM36672P/STK3013 to `net.hadess.SensorProxy` over D-Bus | implemented |
| `j7elte-power` | power_supply/UPower integration, capacity_max restore | implemented |
| `j7elte-fde` | unl0kr/fbdev initramfs integration for FDE | implemented |
| `j7elte-gpsd` | BCM4752 power + NMEA PTY/socket forwarder | partial: init protocol blocked |
| `j7elte-cam` | minimal V4L2/media-controller capture client | implemented (basic capture only) |
| `j7elte-cbd` | CP boot loader for `/dev/umts_boot0` | partial: RIL layer blocked |
| `firmware-samsung-j7elte` | Wi-Fi/BT/FIMC-IS/MFC blobs | implemented |

Details and test plans are in `parity/reports/*-userspace.md`.

## Second-round verification

- 14 pmaports patches (firmware, kernel config, all userspace packages, device deps)
  apply cleanly in order to a fresh `ba682bd` worktree.
- Combined kernel build with camera + Bluetooth + DRM patches and the DRM config
  fragment: `BUILD_EXIT=0`, `Image` 17,545,608 B, three DTBs.
- The built Image contains the camera `request_firmware` fallback and the
  `samsung,exynos7580-decon-drm` compatible; the built DTB routes `bluetooth`
  pinctrl to `gpc4-2` and contains the DRM display compatibles.
- Verification is static plus cross-build; no phone was available for runtime tests.

## Remaining blockers

- **GPU / 3D**: the kernel exposes only kbase; Mesa/Panfrost needs a mainline DRM
  driver. No Linux Mali-T720 userspace exists for this kernel. Software rendering
  (llvmpipe) is the only usable path.
- **Telephony (calls/SMS/data)**: the CP loader is implemented and dry-run verified,
  but the Samsung SIPC5 RIL is proprietary and undocumented.
- **GPS**: power/NMEA forwarding works, but the BCM4752 init exchange is proprietary;
  a hardware capture is required to finish it.
- **Camera**: basic capture only; 3A/JPEG HAL is not implemented.
- **Display**: the DRM/KMS driver compiles; a hardware modeset is still untested.

## Notes

- The original stock zip remains at `/home/asdf/Downloads/SAMFW.COM_SM-J700M_PCW_J700MUBU2BRC2_fac.zip`.
- 218 scratch entries moved from `/tmp` to `session/tmp-artifacts/` (see `MANIFEST.txt`).
- Verification is static plus cross-build; no runtime test on the phone was possible here.

# Maintainer: j7elte parity work <parity@example.invalid>
#
# Minimal still-frame capture client for the FIMC-IS2 pipeline of the
# Samsung Galaxy J7 (j7elte, Exynos 7580).  The kernel driver
# (CONFIG_VIDEO_EXYNOS_FIMC_IS, linux-samsung-j7elte) exposes Samsung's
# camera-HAL video nodes (exynos-fimc-is-ss0/ss1, 30s/30c, 31s/31c, i0s, scp)
# rather than a media-controller graph, so a generic V4L2 client cannot use
# it.  j7elte-cam drives those nodes directly, copies one SCP frame out and
# writes it as PPM/raw.  It is a diagnostic/imager tool, not a camera HAL:
# there is no 3A loop and no JPEG encoder.
#
# Runtime requirements:
#   - firmware-samsung-j7elte installed (/lib/firmware/fimc_is_fw2_3l2.bin,
#     setfile_3l2.bin, setfile_5e3.bin, fimc_is_fd.bin)
#   - the user must be able to open /dev/video* (group "video")
# See parity/reports/camera-userspace.md.

pkgver=1.0.0
pkgrel=0
pkgdesc="FIMC-IS still-frame capture client for the Samsung Galaxy J7 (j7elte)"
url="https://postmarketos.org"
arch="aarch64"
license="MIT"

subpackages=""
builddir="$srcdir"
source="

	j7elte-cam.c

arguments.content:
# Camera userspace: j7elte-cam

Status: **implemented (basic still capture only)**. Kernel drive is at parity;
the remaining scope is deliberate: no 3A loop and no JPEG/HAL.

## Kernel interface

The Nura `fimc-is2` driver exposes Samsung's camera-HAL video nodes rather than
a standard media-controller graph.  `j7elte-cam` therefore enumerates
`/dev/video*` through `/sys/class/video4linux/videoN/name` and selects the
FIMC-IS nodes by role:

- rear S5K3L2: `exynos-fimc-is-ss0`, `30s/30c`, `31s/31c`, `i0s`, `scp`
- front S5K5E3: `ss1/31s/31c/i0s/scp` (`--front`)

The driver registers no `media_device`, and several ioctl handlers are stubs
(`QUERYCAP`/`ENUM_FMT`/`G_FMT` on some nodes return 0 without filling the
structure), so the client never relies on them for identification or format
negotiation.  Frames are dequeued from the SCP node and converted to PPM.

## Tool

`parity/userspace/camera/j7elte-cam/j7elte-cam.c` (single C file, no non-POSIX
dependencies) supports:

```
-l, --list                 list video/media nodes
-o, --output FILE          PPM (P6) output
-r, --raw FILE             raw Y/Cb/Cr planes
-s, --sensor-size WxH[@FPS] sensor mode (default 2072x1552@30)
-O, --out-size WxH         SCP output (default 1280x720, width % 16 == 0)
-n, --buffers N            3..8 (default 4)
-t, --timeout SEC          default 15
-f, --front                front S5K5E3
-m, --memory MODE          otf (default) or dma
    --range MODE           full (default) or limited
    --hal-version VER      1.0 or 3.2 (default 3.2)
```

## Build and package

- Cross-compiled cleanly with the session's GCC 10.3 aarch64 toolchain:
  `aarch64-none-linux-gnu-gcc -O2 -pipe -Wall -Wextra -std=gnu11 ...`
- pmaports package `j7elte-cam` (APKBUILD + sources) under
  `parity/pmaports/device/archived/j7elte-cam/`.
- Exported patch:
  `parity/patches/userspace/camera/0001-pmaports-add-j7elte-cam-package.patch`
  (`git apply --check` against pmaports `ba682bd` passes).
- Runtime dependencies: `firmware-samsung-j7elte` (FIMC-IS firmware/setfiles)
  and read access to `/dev/video*` (group `video`).

## Verification

- Source rebuilt from the packaged copy; no warnings.
- Patch applies to a clean pmaports tree; package sources match the APKBUILD
  checksums.
- No hardware was available, so no frame was captured.  This is a static and
  cross-build verification only.

## Hardware test plan

1. Install `linux-samsung-j7elte`, `firmware-samsung-j7elte`, `j7elte-cam`.
2. `j7elte-cam --list`; confirm the rear/front node names.
3. `j7elte-cam -o rear.ppm` and `j7elte-cam --front -o front.ppm`.
4. Check the PPM images and `dmesg` for FIMC-IS errors; test 640x480 and
   1280x720, `--memory dma`, and power-cycle/suspend-resume.

## Limitations

- No 3A (auto exposure/focus/white balance) and no JPEG encoder; the tool
  captures one raw frame.
- The FIMC-IS ioctl surface is Samsung-specific and partly stubbed; the client
  is intentionally diagnostic rather than a camera HAL.
- Firmware and sensor calibration (`/efs`) must be present for the pipeline to
  start.

# DRM/KMS driver: exynos7580

Status: **implemented and compiled; hardware modeset untested**.

## What was added

New driver `drivers/gpu/drm/exynos7580/`:

- `exynos7580_drm.c` - DRM device, mode config, CMA GEM/dumb buffers, fbdev
  emulation, vblank, legacy CRTC helpers.
- `exynos7580_decon.c` - DECON CRTC + primary plane; register access, clocks,
  power domain, scanout setup.
- `exynos7580_dsim.c` - MIPI DSIM master/D-PHY, encoder and connector; panel
  enable/disable sequencing.
- `exynos7580_drm.h` - shared state and prototypes.
- `Kconfig`/`Makefile` integration under `drivers/gpu/drm/`.

DT binding (rev00/04/06):

```
decon_fb@14830000 { compatible = "samsung,exynos7580-decon-drm"; ... };
dsim@14800000     { compatible = "samsung,exynos7580-dsim"; ... };
```

The driver finds the DSIM node via `of_find_compatible_node()` and uses the
existing `ea8061_wxga` panel, `decon_board_list` reset/power sequences,
clocks, regulators and power domains already present in the vendor DT.

## Configuration

`parity/patches/drm/config-drm-exynos7580.fragment`:

```
CONFIG_DRM=y
CONFIG_DRM_KMS_HELPER=y
CONFIG_DRM_KMS_CMA_HELPER=y
CONFIG_DRM_EXYNOS7580=y
CONFIG_FRAMEBUFFER_CONSOLE=y
CONFIG_CMA_SIZE_MBYTES=32
# vendor fbdev path disabled
```

The vendor fbdev display stack and this driver claim the same DECON/DSIM
hardware; they must not both be enabled.  The fragment is opt-in so the vendor
fbdev path remains the fallback until the DRM modeset is validated.

## Build verification

Applied to a clean `b5e363a` worktree together with the pmaports build patches,
the camera patch, the Bluetooth DT patch and the DRM config fragment:

```
parity/final-out/arch/arm64/boot/Image   17,545,608 bytes
parity/final-out/arch/arm64/boot/dts/exynos7580-j7elte_rev00.dtb
parity/final-out/arch/arm64/boot/dts/exynos7580-j7elte_rev04.dtb
parity/final-out/arch/arm64/boot/dts/exynos7580-j7elte_rev06.dtb
```

Built objects:

```
drivers/gpu/drm/exynos7580/exynos7580_drm.o
drivers/gpu/drm/exynos7580/exynos7580_decon.o
drivers/gpu/drm/exynos7580/exynos7580_dsim.o
```

The built Image contains `samsung,exynos7580-decon-drm`; the built DTB contains
the DECON/DSIM compatibles and the BT `gpc4-2` group.

Patches (apply-checked against `b5e363a`):

- `parity/patches/drm/0001-drm-exynos7580-decon-dsim-kms.patch`
- `parity/patches/drm/0002-arm64-dts-exynos7580-j7elte-drm-display.patch`

## Design notes

- 3.10 has no atomic helpers; the driver uses the legacy CRTC/encoder/connector
  helpers and a single primary plane.  This is sufficient for a KMS compositor
  using the legacy modeset path; modern atomic-only compositors may need
  additional work.
- CMA is used for dumb buffers (`drm_gem_cma_*`).  The stock config had
  `CONFIG_CMA_SIZE_MBYTES=0`; the fragment reserves 32 MB.
- The driver does not implement HDMI, overlays, rotation or the vendor MDNIE
  color path; the ea8061 panel init sequence and DECON register values are
  taken from the vendor `decon_7580` driver.
- The vendor fbdev driver remains available if the DRM path is disabled.

## Hardware test plan

1. Build with the DRM fragment; flash the resulting boot image.
2. Check `dmesg` for `exynos7580-drm` probe, DECON/DSIM clocks and panel init.
3. Confirm `/dev/dri/card0`; run `modetest -M exynos7580` or `weston`.
4. Verify 720x1280 modeset, fbdev console, suspend/resume and backlight.
5. If the panel stays black, capture the DSIM/DECON register state and compare
   with the vendor fbdev driver; the fallback is to re-enable the vendor path.

## Risks

- No hardware validation of the modeset; the panel power/reset timing is the
  most likely failure point.
- Legacy non-atomic KMS may not satisfy compositors that require atomic modeset.
- 32 MB CMA may be tight for large buffers; tune for the compositor used.
- Disabling the vendor fbdev driver also removes its framebuffer console until
  the DRM fbdev emulation takes over.

# j7elte ROM <-> Nura driver parity session

Working directory for the Samsung Galaxy J7 (2015) `SM-J700M` (`j7elte`, Exynos 7580)
kernel driver parity work between the stock Android ROM and Nura (formerly postmarketOS).

## Device / sources

- Stock ROM: `SM-J700M` `J700MUBU2BRC2`, Android 6.0.1, kernel `3.10.61-13213628`.
- ROM kernel: raw arm64 `Image`, all drivers built in (no `.ko` modules),
  55,634 kallsyms symbols recovered.
- Nura kernel: `LineageOS/android_kernel_samsung_universal7580` @ `2a746c1`,
  downstream 3.10.108, baseline commit `b5e363a`. Nura is **not** mainline for this device.
- Upstream reference: Linux 7.3 (kernel.org), used only for the parity survey.

## Layout

```
boot.img, recovery.img, system.img, system.raw   extracted ROM images
AP_J700MUBU2BRC2_..._user_low_ship.tar.md5       AP tar (extracted from the stock zip)
boot_out/                                        kernel.bin, vmlinux.elf, symbols.txt, dtbs/
android_kernel_samsung_universal7580-.../         Nura kernel tree (clean baseline)
linux-7.3/, linux-7.3.tar.xz                      upstream reference
toolchains/                                       GCC 10.3 aarch64 toolchain
config-nura-j7elte                                Nura build config (pristine)
lineage-kernel.tar.gz                             Nura kernel source archive
tools/                                            boot image / config comparison helpers
session/tmp-artifacts/                            scratch files moved out of /tmp
parity/                                           all deliverables (see below)
```

`parity/`:

```
patches/          7 exported patches (kernel + pmaports)
reports/          14 per-driver reports (P1-P4 evidence)
firmware/         extracted ROM blobs + per-driver file lists + MANIFEST.sha512
pmaports/         pmaports baseline ba682bd + uncommitted integration changes
build-src/        kernel worktree with build patches + parity kernel patches applied
out/              built Image and rev00/rev04/rev06 DTBs
build.sh          kernel build script (GCC 10.3)
verify.sh         applies every patch with git apply --check against the baselines
contract.md       parity definition and evidence rules
*.log             baseline / camera / final build logs
```

## Patches

Kernel (apply to the baseline kernel tree):

1. `parity/patches/bluetooth/0001-j7elte-bt-pinctrl.patch`
   - BT enable pin was `gpa1-6`; ROM uses `gpc4-2` on all three board revisions.
2. `parity/patches/camera/0001-fimc-is2-fallback-to-request_firmware-for-fw-version-check.patch`
   - FIMC-IS firmware version check hard-failed on `/system/vendor/firmware`;
     add a `request_firmware()` fallback so `/lib/firmware` works.

pmaports (apply in this order to `parity/pmaports`, baseline `ba682bd`):

3. `parity/patches/wifi/0001-j7elte-wifi-firmware-paths.patch`
   - `BCMDHD_FW_PATH` / `BCMDHD_NVRAM_PATH` -> `/lib/firmware/postmarketos/samsung-j7elte/`.
4. `parity/patches/bluetooth/0002-j7elte-bt-hci-config.patch`
   - enable `CONFIG_BT_HCIUART` + `CONFIG_BT_HCIUART_H4` for BlueZ `hciattach`/`btattach`.
5. `parity/patches/pmaports/0003-firmware-samsung-j7elte-package.patch`
   - new `firmware-samsung-j7elte` package (Wi-Fi, BT, FIMC-IS, MFC blobs).
6. `parity/patches/pmaports/0004-device-samsung-j7elte-depend-firmware.patch`
   - device package depends on the firmware package.
7. `parity/patches/pmaports/0005-linux-samsung-j7elte-config-sha512.patch`
   - updated config checksum after the two config changes.

```

./verify.sh          # all 7 patches -> OK
```

fix-argb, etc.) plus the two parity kernel patches:

```

./parity/build.sh parity/build-src parity/out Image dtbs
```

```
parity/out/arch/arm64/boot/Image
parity/out/arch/arm64/boot/dts/exynos7580-j7elte_rev00.dtb
parity/out/arch/arm64/boot/dts/exynos7580-j7elte_rev04.dtb
parity/out/arch/arm64/boot/dts/exynos7580-j7elte_rev06.dtb
```

Final build status: `BUILD_EXIT=0`, Image 17,365,040 bytes, three DTBs.
The camera fallback string and the `gpc4-2` BT pin group are present in the built outputs.

## Firmware package

`parity/pmaports/device/archived/firmware-samsung-j7elte/` contains:

- `APKBUILD` (deterministic `firmware.tar.gz`, sha512 pinned)
- `extract-firmware.sh` (rebuilds the tarball from the stock AP tar; verifies `files.sha512`)
- `files.sha512` (per-blob checksums)

Install destinations:

- `/lib/firmware/postmarketos/samsung-j7elte/` - bcmdhd firmware/NVRAM, BT HCD
- `/lib/firmware/` - `fimc_is_fw2_3l2.bin`, `setfile_3l2.bin`, `setfile_5e3.bin`,
  `fimc_is_fd.bin`, `mfc_fw.bin`

## Kernel driver parity (first round)

- 11 driver families at parity: display, battery, audio, sensors, storage, touch,
  USB, GPS, GPU, platform (thermal/devfreq/IOMMU/cpufreq), modem.
- 3 driver families patched: Wi-Fi (config), Bluetooth (DT + config), camera (driver fallback).
- The ROM's driver set is already present in the Nura fork; no driver code was missing
  for those families.

## New DRM/KMS driver (display)

- `parity/patches/drm/0001-drm-exynos7580-decon-dsim-kms.patch`
  adds `drivers/gpu/drm/exynos7580/` (DECON CRTC/plane, DSIM encoder/connector,
  ea8061 panel init, dumb buffers + fbdev).
- `parity/patches/drm/0002-arm64-dts-exynos7580-j7elte-drm-display.patch`
  adds `samsung,exynos7580-decon-drm` / `samsung,exynos7580-dsim` to rev00/04/06.
- `parity/patches/drm/config-drm-exynos7580.fragment` enables DRM,
  `CONFIG_DRM_EXYNOS7580`, 32 MB CMA, and disables the vendor fbdev display path.
- Verified build: `parity/final-out/arch/arm64/boot/Image` (17,545,608 B) + three
  j7elte DTBs; `exynos7580_{drm,decon,dsim}.o` are built and the DTBs contain the
  new compatibles.
- Hardware-untested. Keep the vendor fbdev driver as the fallback until a real
  modeset is validated on the phone.

## Userspace gap packages

New pmaports packages, all pulled in by `device-samsung-j7elte` depends:

| Package | Gap | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `j7elte-audio-ucm` | UCM2 routing/mixer for COD3022X (54/54 controls validated) | implemented |
| `j7elte-wifi` | wpa_supplicant template, `/efs/wifi` MAC provisioning | implemented |
| `j7elte-bt` | rfkill + hciattach + bluetoothd service, BCM43438A1.hcd | implemented |
| `j7elte-sensors` | K2HH/CM36672P/STK3013 to `net.hadess.SensorProxy` over D-Bus | implemented |
| `j7elte-power` | power_supply/UPower integration, capacity_max restore | implemented |
| `j7elte-fde` | unl0kr/fbdev initramfs integration for FDE | implemented |
| `j7elte-gpsd` | BCM4752 power + NMEA PTY/socket forwarder | partial: init protocol blocked |
| `j7elte-cam` | minimal V4L2/media-controller capture client | implemented (basic capture only) |
| `j7elte-cbd` | CP boot loader for `/dev/umts_boot0` | partial: RIL layer blocked |
| `firmware-samsung-j7elte` | Wi-Fi/BT/FIMC-IS/MFC blobs | implemented |

Details and test plans are in `parity/reports/*-userspace.md`.

## Second-round verification

- 14 pmaports patches (firmware, kernel config, all userspace packages, device deps)
  apply cleanly in order to a fresh `ba682bd` worktree.
- Combined kernel build with camera + Bluetooth + DRM patches and the DRM config
  fragment: `BUILD_EXIT=0`, `Image` 17,545,608 B, three DTBs.
- The built Image contains the camera `request_firmware` fallback and the
  `samsung,exynos7580-decon-drm` compatible; the built DTB routes `bluetooth`
  pinctrl to `gpc4-2` and contains the DRM display compatibles.
- Verification is static plus cross-build; no phone was available for runtime tests.

## Remaining blockers

- **GPU / 3D**: the kernel exposes only kbase; Mesa/Panfrost needs a mainline DRM
  driver. No Linux Mali-T720 userspace exists for this kernel. Software rendering
  (llvmpipe) is the only usable path.
- **Telephony (calls/SMS/data)**: the CP loader is implemented and dry-run verified,
  but the Samsung SIPC5 RIL is proprietary and undocumented.
- **GPS**: power/NMEA forwarding works, but the BCM4752 init exchange is proprietary;
  a hardware capture is required to finish it.
- **Camera**: basic capture only; 3A/JPEG HAL is not implemented.
- **Display**: the DRM/KMS driver compiles; a hardware modeset is still untested.

## Notes

- The original stock zip remains at `/home/asdf/Downloads/SAMFW.COM_SM-J700M_PCW_J700MUBU2BRC2_fac.zip`.
- 218 scratch entries moved from `/tmp` to `session/tmp-artifacts/` (see `MANIFEST.txt`).
- Verification is static plus cross-build; no runtime test on the phone was possible here.

# j7elte ROM <-> Nura driver parity session

Working directory for the Samsung Galaxy J7 (2015) `SM-J700M` (`j7elte`, Exynos 7580)
kernel driver parity work between the stock Android ROM and Nura (formerly postmarketOS).

## Device / sources

- Stock ROM: `SM-J700M` `J700MUBU2BRC2`, Android 6.0.1, kernel `3.10.61-13213628`.
- ROM kernel: raw arm64 `Image`, all drivers built in (no `.ko` modules),
  55,634 kallsyms symbols recovered.
- Nura kernel: `LineageOS/android_kernel_samsung_universal7580` @ `2a746c1`,
  downstream 3.10.108, baseline commit `b5e363a`. Nura is **not** mainline for this device.
- Upstream reference: Linux 7.3 (kernel.org), used only for the parity survey.

## Layout

```
boot.img, recovery.img, system.img, system.raw   extracted ROM images
AP_J700MUBU2BRC2_..._user_low_ship.tar.md5       AP tar (extracted from the stock zip)
boot_out/                                        kernel.bin, vmlinux.elf, symbols.txt, dtbs/
android_kernel_samsung_universal7580-.../         Nura kernel tree (clean baseline)
linux-7.3/, linux-7.3.tar.xz                      upstream reference
toolchains/                                       GCC 10.3 aarch64 toolchain
config-nura-j7elte                                Nura build config (pristine)
lineage-kernel.tar.gz                             Nura kernel source archive
tools/                                            boot image / config comparison helpers
session/tmp-artifacts/                            scratch files moved out of /tmp
parity/                                           all deliverables (see below)
```

`parity/`:

```
patches/          7 exported patches (kernel + pmaports)
reports/          14 per-driver reports (P1-P4 evidence)
firmware/         extracted ROM blobs + per-driver file lists + MANIFEST.sha512
pmaports/         pmaports baseline ba682bd + uncommitted integration changes
build-src/        kernel worktree with build patches + parity kernel patches applied
out/              built Image and rev00/rev04/rev06 DTBs
build.sh          kernel build script (GCC 10.3)
verify.sh         applies every patch with git apply --check against the baselines
contract.md       parity definition and evidence rules
*.log             baseline / camera / final build logs
```

## Patches

Kernel (apply to the baseline kernel tree, commit `b5e363a`):

1. `parity/patches/bluetooth/0001-j7elte-bt-pinctrl.patch`
   - BT enable pin was `gpa1-6`; ROM uses `gpc4-2` on all three board revisions.
2. `parity/patches/camera/0001-fimc-is2-fallback-to-request_firmware-for-fw-version-check.patch`
   - FIMC-IS firmware version check hard-failed on `/system/vendor/firmware`;
     add a `request_firmware()` fallback so `/lib/firmware` works.
3. `parity/patches/drm/0001-drm-exynos7580-decon-dsim-kms.patch`
   - new `drivers/gpu/drm/exynos7580/` KMS driver (DECON + DSIM + ea8061).
4. `parity/patches/drm/0002-arm64-dts-exynos7580-j7elte-drm-display.patch`
   - DT compatibles for the DRM driver on rev00/04/06.

pmaports (apply in this order to `parity/pmaports`, baseline `ba682bd`):

5. `parity/patches/wifi/0001-j7elte-wifi-firmware-paths.patch`
   - `BCMDHD_FW_PATH` / `BCMDHD_NVRAM_PATH` -> `/lib/firmware/postmarketos/samsung-j7elte/`.
6. `parity/patches/bluetooth/0002-j7elte-bt-hci-config.patch`
   - enable `CONFIG_BT_HCIUART` + `CONFIG_BT_HCIUART_H4` for BlueZ.
7. `parity/patches/pmaports/0003-firmware-samsung-j7elte-package.patch`
   - new `firmware-samsung-j7elte` package (Wi-Fi, BT, FIMC-IS, MFC blobs).
8. `parity/patches/pmaports/0005-linux-samsung-j7elte-config-sha512.patch`
   - updated config checksum after the two config changes.
9. `parity/patches/userspace/0001-device-deps.patch`
   - `device-samsung-j7elte` depends on the firmware and all userspace packages.
10. `parity/patches/userspace/audio/0002-j7elte-audio-ucm-package.patch`
11. `parity/patches/userspace/connectivity/0001-j7elte-wifi-package.patch`
12. `parity/patches/userspace/connectivity/0002-j7elte-bt-package.patch`
13. `parity/patches/userspace/sensors/0001-add-j7elte-sensors-package.patch`
14. `parity/patches/userspace/battery/0001-pmaports-add-j7elte-power-package.patch`
15. `parity/patches/userspace/gps/0001-pmaports-add-j7elte-gpsd-package.patch`
16. `parity/patches/userspace/ril/0001-j7elte-cbd-package.patch`
17. `parity/patches/userspace/camera/0001-pmaports-add-j7elte-cam-package.patch`
18. `parity/patches/userspace/fde/0001-j7elte-fde-package.patch`

DRM config fragment (opt-in, used for the final build):
`parity/patches/drm/config-drm-exynos7580.fragment`.

Verify everything:

```
cd parity
./verify.sh          # 18 patches OK; 1 source-tree patch skipped
```

## Build

The ready-to-build worktree already contains the pmaports build patches (gcc8/gcc10,
fix-argb, etc.) plus the two parity kernel patches:

```
cd j7elte-session
./parity/build.sh parity/build-src parity/out Image dtbs
```

Outputs:

```
parity/out/arch/arm64/boot/Image
parity/out/arch/arm64/boot/dts/exynos7580-j7elte_rev00.dtb
parity/out/arch/arm64/boot/dts/exynos7580-j7elte_rev04.dtb
parity/out/arch/arm64/boot/dts/exynos7580-j7elte_rev06.dtb
```

Final build status: `BUILD_EXIT=0`, Image 17,365,040 bytes, three DTBs.
The camera fallback string and the `gpc4-2` BT pin group are present in the built outputs.

## Firmware package

`parity/pmaports/device/archived/firmware-samsung-j7elte/` contains:

- `APKBUILD` (deterministic `firmware.tar.gz`, sha512 pinned)
- `extract-firmware.sh` (rebuilds the tarball from the stock AP tar; verifies `files.sha512`)
- `files.sha512` (per-blob checksums)

Install destinations:

- `/lib/firmware/postmarketos/samsung-j7elte/` - bcmdhd firmware/NVRAM, BT HCD
- `/lib/firmware/` - `fimc_is_fw2_3l2.bin`, `setfile_3l2.bin`, `setfile_5e3.bin`,
  `fimc_is_fd.bin`, `mfc_fw.bin`

## Kernel driver parity (first round)

- 11 driver families at parity: display, battery, audio, sensors, storage, touch,
  USB, GPS, GPU, platform (thermal/devfreq/IOMMU/cpufreq), modem.
- 3 driver families patched: Wi-Fi (config), Bluetooth (DT + config), camera (driver fallback).
- The ROM's driver set is already present in the Nura fork; no driver code was missing
  for those families.

## New DRM/KMS driver (display)

- `parity/patches/drm/0001-drm-exynos7580-decon-dsim-kms.patch`
  adds `drivers/gpu/drm/exynos7580/` (DECON CRTC/plane, DSIM encoder/connector,
  ea8061 panel init, dumb buffers + fbdev).
- `parity/patches/drm/0002-arm64-dts-exynos7580-j7elte-drm-display.patch`
  adds `samsung,exynos7580-decon-drm` / `samsung,exynos7580-dsim` to rev00/04/06.
- `parity/patches/drm/config-drm-exynos7580.fragment` enables DRM,
  `CONFIG_DRM_EXYNOS7580`, 32 MB CMA, and disables the vendor fbdev display path.
- Verified build: `parity/final-out/arch/arm64/boot/Image` (17,545,608 B) + three
  j7elte DTBs; `exynos7580_{drm,decon,dsim}.o` are built and the DTBs contain the
  new compatibles.
- Hardware-untested. Keep the vendor fbdev driver as the fallback until a real
  modeset is validated on the phone.

## Userspace gap packages

New pmaports packages, all pulled in by `device-samsung-j7elte` depends:

| Package | Gap | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `j7elte-audio-ucm` | UCM2 routing/mixer for COD3022X (54/54 controls validated) | implemented |
| `j7elte-wifi` | wpa_supplicant template, `/efs/wifi` MAC provisioning | implemented |
| `j7elte-bt` | rfkill + hciattach + bluetoothd service, BCM43438A1.hcd | implemented |
| `j7elte-sensors` | K2HH/CM36672P/STK3013 to `net.hadess.SensorProxy` over D-Bus | implemented |
| `j7elte-power` | power_supply/UPower integration, capacity_max restore | implemented |
| `j7elte-fde` | unl0kr/fbdev initramfs integration for FDE | implemented |
| `j7elte-gpsd` | BCM4752 power + NMEA PTY/socket forwarder | partial: init protocol blocked |
| `j7elte-cam` | minimal V4L2/media-controller capture client | implemented (basic capture only) |
| `j7elte-cbd` | CP boot loader for `/dev/umts_boot0` | partial: RIL layer blocked |
| `firmware-samsung-j7elte` | Wi-Fi/BT/FIMC-IS/MFC blobs | implemented |

Details and test plans are in `parity/reports/*-userspace.md`.

## Second-round verification

- 14 pmaports patches (firmware, kernel config, all userspace packages, device deps)
  apply cleanly in order to a fresh `ba682bd` worktree.
- Combined kernel build with camera + Bluetooth + DRM patches and the DRM config
  fragment: `BUILD_EXIT=0`, `Image` 17,545,608 B, three DTBs.
- The built Image contains the camera `request_firmware` fallback and the
  `samsung,exynos7580-decon-drm` compatible; the built DTB routes `bluetooth`
  pinctrl to `gpc4-2` and contains the DRM display compatibles.
- Verification is static plus cross-build; no phone was available for runtime tests.

## Remaining blockers

- **GPU / 3D**: the kernel exposes only kbase; Mesa/Panfrost needs a mainline DRM
  driver. No Linux Mali-T720 userspace exists for this kernel. Software rendering
  (llvmpipe) is the only usable path.
- **Telephony (calls/SMS/data)**: the CP loader is implemented and dry-run verified,
  but the Samsung SIPC5 RIL is proprietary and undocumented.
- **GPS**: power/NMEA forwarding works, but the BCM4752 init exchange is proprietary;
  a hardware capture is required to finish it.
- **Camera**: basic capture only; 3A/JPEG HAL is not implemented.
- **Display**: the DRM/KMS driver compiles; a hardware modeset is still untested.

## Notes

- The original stock zip remains at `/home/asdf/Downloads/SAMFW.COM_SM-J700M_PCW_J700MUBU2BRC2_fac.zip`.
- 218 scratch entries moved from `/tmp` to `session/tmp-artifacts/` (see `MANIFEST.txt`).
- Verification is static plus cross-build; no runtime test on the phone was possible here.

# j7elte ROM <-> Nura driver parity session

Working directory for the Samsung Galaxy J7 (2015) `SM-J700M` (`j7elte`, Exynos 7580)
kernel driver parity work between the stock Android ROM and Nura (formerly postmarketOS).

## Device / sources

- Stock ROM: `SM-J700M` `J700MUBU2BRC2`, Android 6.0.1, kernel `3.10.61-13213628`.
- ROM kernel: raw arm64 `Image`, all drivers built in (no `.ko` modules),
  55,634 kallsyms symbols recovered.
- Nura kernel: `LineageOS/android_kernel_samsung_universal7580` @ `2a746c1`,
  downstream 3.10.108, baseline commit `b5e363a`. Nura is **not** mainline for this device.
- Upstream reference: Linux 7.3 (kernel.org), used only for the parity survey.

## Layout

```
boot.img, recovery.img, system.img, system.raw   extracted ROM images
AP_J700MUBU2BRC2_..._user_low_ship.tar.md5       AP tar (extracted from the stock zip)
boot_out/                                        kernel.bin, vmlinux.elf, symbols.txt, dtbs/
android_kernel_samsung_universal7580-.../         Nura kernel tree (clean baseline)
linux-7.3/, linux-7.3.tar.xz                      upstream reference
toolchains/                                       GCC 10.3 aarch64 toolchain
config-nura-j7elte                                Nura build config (pristine)
lineage-kernel.tar.gz                             Nura kernel source archive
tools/                                            boot image / config comparison helpers
session/tmp-artifacts/                            scratch files moved out of /tmp
parity/                                           all deliverables (see below)
```

`parity/`:

```
patches/          7 exported patches (kernel + pmaports)
reports/          14 per-driver reports (P1-P4 evidence)
firmware/         extracted ROM blobs + per-driver file lists + MANIFEST.sha512
pmaports/         pmaports baseline ba682bd + uncommitted integration changes
build-src/        kernel worktree with build patches + parity kernel patches applied
out/              built Image and rev00/rev04/rev06 DTBs
build.sh          kernel build script (GCC 10.3)
verify.sh         applies every patch with git apply --check against the baselines
contract.md       parity definition and evidence rules
*.log             baseline / camera / final build logs
```

## Patches

Kernel (apply to the baseline kernel tree, commit `b5e363a`):

1. `parity/patches/bluetooth/0001-j7elte-bt-pinctrl.patch`
   - BT enable pin was `gpa1-6`; ROM uses `gpc4-2` on all three board revisions.
2. `parity/patches/camera/0001-fimc-is2-fallback-to-request_firmware-for-fw-version-check.patch`
   - FIMC-IS firmware version check hard-failed on `/system/vendor/firmware`;
     add a `request_firmware()` fallback so `/lib/firmware` works.
3. `parity/patches/drm/0001-drm-exynos7580-decon-dsim-kms.patch`
   - new `drivers/gpu/drm/exynos7580/` KMS driver (DECON + DSIM + ea8061).
4. `parity/patches/drm/0002-arm64-dts-exynos7580-j7elte-drm-display.patch`
   - DT compatibles for the DRM driver on rev00/04/06.

pmaports (apply in this order to `parity/pmaports`, baseline `ba682bd`):

5. `parity/patches/wifi/0001-j7elte-wifi-firmware-paths.patch`
   - `BCMDHD_FW_PATH` / `BCMDHD_NVRAM_PATH` -> `/lib/firmware/postmarketos/samsung-j7elte/`.
6. `parity/patches/bluetooth/0002-j7elte-bt-hci-config.patch`
   - enable `CONFIG_BT_HCIUART` + `CONFIG_BT_HCIUART_H4` for BlueZ.
7. `parity/patches/pmaports/0003-firmware-samsung-j7elte-package.patch`
   - new `firmware-samsung-j7elte` package (Wi-Fi, BT, FIMC-IS, MFC blobs).
8. `parity/patches/pmaports/0005-linux-samsung-j7elte-config-sha512.patch`
   - updated config checksum after the two config changes.
9. `parity/patches/userspace/0001-device-deps.patch`
   - `device-samsung-j7elte` depends on the firmware and all userspace packages.
10. `parity/patches/userspace/audio/0002-j7elte-audio-ucm-package.patch`
11. `parity/patches/userspace/connectivity/0001-j7elte-wifi-package.patch`
12. `parity/patches/userspace/connectivity/0002-j7elte-bt-package.patch`
13. `parity/patches/userspace/sensors/0001-add-j7elte-sensors-package.patch`
14. `parity/patches/userspace/battery/0001-pmaports-add-j7elte-power-package.patch`
15. `parity/patches/userspace/gps/0001-pmaports-add-j7elte-gpsd-package.patch`
16. `parity/patches/userspace/ril/0001-j7elte-cbd-package.patch`
17. `parity/patches/userspace/camera/0001-pmaports-add-j7elte-cam-package.patch`
18. `parity/patches/userspace/fde/0001-j7elte-fde-package.patch`

DRM config fragment (opt-in, used for the final build):
`parity/patches/drm/config-drm-exynos7580.fragment`.

Verify everything:

```
cd parity
./verify.sh          # 18 patches OK; 1 source-tree patch skipped
```

## Build

Base build (vendor fbdev display, camera + BT patches):

```
./parity/build.sh parity/build-src parity/out Image dtbs
```

Result: `BUILD_EXIT=0`, Image 17,365,040 B, three j7elte DTBs under `parity/out/`.

Final combined build (adds the DRM/KMS driver; opt-in config):

```
CFG=parity/final-config ./parity/build.sh parity/final-kernel-check parity/final-out Image dtbs
```

- `parity/final-kernel-check` is a clean `b5e363a` worktree with the pmaports
  build patches (GCC 10, fix-argb, sun/Solaris flag, etc.) plus the Bluetooth,
  camera and DRM kernel patches.
- `parity/final-config` is the WiFi/BT kernel config plus
  `parity/patches/drm/config-drm-exynos7580.fragment` (DRM, 32 MB CMA, vendor
  fbdev display path disabled).
- Result: `BUILD_EXIT=0`, Image **17,545,608 B**, three j7elte DTBs under
  `parity/final-out/`, `exynos7580_{drm,decon,dsim}.o` built, camera fallback
  and BT `gpc4-2` group present in the outputs.

Keep the vendor fbdev path as the fallback; do not enable both display stacks
at once.

## Firmware package

`parity/pmaports/device/archived/firmware-samsung-j7elte/` contains:

- `APKBUILD` (deterministic `firmware.tar.gz`, sha512 pinned)
- `extract-firmware.sh` (rebuilds the tarball from the stock AP tar; verifies `files.sha512`)
- `files.sha512` (per-blob checksums)

Install destinations:

- `/lib/firmware/postmarketos/samsung-j7elte/` - bcmdhd firmware/NVRAM, BT HCD
- `/lib/firmware/` - `fimc_is_fw2_3l2.bin`, `setfile_3l2.bin`, `setfile_5e3.bin`,
  `fimc_is_fd.bin`, `mfc_fw.bin`

## Kernel driver parity (first round)

- 11 driver families at parity: display, battery, audio, sensors, storage, touch,
  USB, GPS, GPU, platform (thermal/devfreq/IOMMU/cpufreq), modem.
- 3 driver families patched: Wi-Fi (config), Bluetooth (DT + config), camera (driver fallback).
- The ROM's driver set is already present in the Nura fork; no driver code was missing
  for those families.

## New DRM/KMS driver (display)

- `parity/patches/drm/0001-drm-exynos7580-decon-dsim-kms.patch`
  adds `drivers/gpu/drm/exynos7580/` (DECON CRTC/plane, DSIM encoder/connector,
  ea8061 panel init, dumb buffers + fbdev).
- `parity/patches/drm/0002-arm64-dts-exynos7580-j7elte-drm-display.patch`
  adds `samsung,exynos7580-decon-drm` / `samsung,exynos7580-dsim` to rev00/04/06.
- `parity/patches/drm/config-drm-exynos7580.fragment` enables DRM,
  `CONFIG_DRM_EXYNOS7580`, 32 MB CMA, and disables the vendor fbdev display path.
- Verified build: `parity/final-out/arch/arm64/boot/Image` (17,545,608 B) + three
  j7elte DTBs; `exynos7580_{drm,decon,dsim}.o` are built and the DTBs contain the
  new compatibles.
- Hardware-untested. Keep the vendor fbdev driver as the fallback until a real
  modeset is validated on the phone.

## Userspace gap packages

New pmaports packages, all pulled in by `device-samsung-j7elte` depends:

| Package | Gap | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `j7elte-audio-ucm` | UCM2 routing/mixer for COD3022X (54/54 controls validated) | implemented |
| `j7elte-wifi` | wpa_supplicant template, `/efs/wifi` MAC provisioning | implemented |
| `j7elte-bt` | rfkill + hciattach + bluetoothd service, BCM43438A1.hcd | implemented |
| `j7elte-sensors` | K2HH/CM36672P/STK3013 to `net.hadess.SensorProxy` over D-Bus | implemented |
| `j7elte-power` | power_supply/UPower integration, capacity_max restore | implemented |
| `j7elte-fde` | unl0kr/fbdev initramfs integration for FDE | implemented |
| `j7elte-gpsd` | BCM4752 power + NMEA PTY/socket forwarder | partial: init protocol blocked |

| `firmware-samsung-j7elte` | Wi-Fi/BT/FIMC-IS/MFC blobs | implemented |

Details and test plans are in `parity/reports/*-userspace.md`.

## Second-round verification

- 14 pmaports patches (firmware, kernel config, all userspace packages, device deps)

- Combined kernel build with camera + Bluetooth + DRM patches and the DRM config
